newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX plans new depositary receipt security.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX plans new depositary receipt security.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Wednesday it plans to introduce a new type of security through its CHESS (Clearing House Electronic Sub-register System), similar to a depositary receipt.

"CUFS (CHESS Units of Foreign Securities) are very similar to traditional depositary receipts issued in offshore markets, except in this case they are issued by a subsidiary of ASX, rather than an international bank," the ASX said.
ASX said Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd is poised to become the first foreign company to be issued CUFS, following its proposed merger with Golden Shamrock Mines Ltd.

CUFS overcame the legal impediments that prevented many foreign companies from participating in CHESS, because the legalislation of their home jurisdiction did not recognise uncertificated holdings and electronic transfers of legal title, the ASX said.
ASX is inviting all listed foreign companines, other than those incorporated in Papua New Guinea (PNG) and New Zealand, to adopt CUFS so that they participate in CHESS, the exchange said.
It said it expected PNG and New Zealand regulatory authorities to allow direct participation in CHESS for companies incorporated in those countries.--Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
